translation.title: Terbinafine Hydrochloride Nail Solution
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for fungal nail infections (onychomycosis) of the fingernails and toenails.
translation.usage: Use it once a day for the first 4 weeks, and once a week after that. Continue applying it until a healthy nail has grown back — generally about 6 months for fingernails and 9 to 12 months for toenails. If the response to this topical treatment is inadequate after the treatment period, or if a serious nail infection appears, including involvement of one or more nail matrices (the tissue under the nail), additional oral (taken-by-mouth) treatment may be needed, so consult a doctor. Apply it to the nails only, and before applying, remove nail polish and other cosmetics from the nail and the immediately adjacent skin. Wash the area clean and dry it completely before use. Using the applicator, spread a thin layer over the entire affected surface and about 5 mm beyond the nail, and where possible under the nail edge and on the skin under the nail, then let it dry for 30 seconds until completely dry. Do not wash or wet the treated nails for at least 6 hours after use, so applying it in the evening before bedtime, after a shower or bath, is recommended; after that time, normal hygiene is possible. To remove this medicine, carefully washing the nails with water is enough — do not use organic solvents or abrasives.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are or have been hypersensitive to terbinafine or to any ingredient of this medicine, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you are breastfeeding, or in children and adolescents under 18. Before using it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if 3 or more nails are affected, if more than half of the nail plate is deformed or the nail matrix is involved, if you have diabetes, an immune disorder or a circulatory disorder (peripheral vascular disease), if your nails are damaged, painful or severely injured, if you have a history of skin disease such as psoriasis or another chronic skin condition, if you have experienced yellow nail syndrome (leg swelling, breathing problems and yellow nails), if you have lesions that alcohol may irritate, or if you have experienced hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to propylene glycol. This medicine is for external use only. Avoid contact between the treated area and other parts of the body until the medicine has dried completely. It may cause irritation if it reaches the eyes or mucous membranes; if it touches the eyes or mucous membranes, rinse them clean with running water. Do not use nail polish or other nail cosmetics while using this medicine. Be careful not to stop the treatment before the recommended period ends — the fungal infection may still remain and the condition may get worse again. If you miss an application, use it as soon as possible in the same way as before; if you only remember at the time of the next application, apply it just once and continue as normal. If you have swallowed this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist or visit a nearby hospital. Do not use other medicines on the affected area while using this medicine. Stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if skin redness or excessive irritation appears or worsens at the application site. This medicine contains ethanol, so a burning feeling may occur on damaged skin.
